value.description: An Eastern-type carrot crop, introduced to Japan from China around the late sixteenth to early seventeenth century. Its long roots can be eaten raw or used in cooking.
Harvested Eastern-type carrots. Their roots can be eaten raw or cooked.

A climbing vine that bears Japanese pumpkins, a type introduced to Japan in the sixteenth century. Their flesh is comparatively moist and less sweet than that of later Western pumpkins, and is suitable for cooking.
Harvested Japanese pumpkins, with relatively moist flesh suited to cooking.
